football_evidence.question: Can Penn State contain Michigan’s explosive runs?
football_evidence.assessment: EdgeDesk’s number is 2.4 points closer to Penn State than the line, and EdgeDesk cannot account for most of that: its own breakdown accounts for about 0.0 of the 2.4 points. The measured football evidence leans toward Michigan, not toward EdgeDesk’s number. Treat the gap as an open research question, not as an edge.
supporting: When Michigan has the ball (big plays through the air): Michigan’s offense turns 9.4% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and Penn State’s defense gives up explosive gains on 5.5% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.4%).

When Michigan has the ball (the passing game against the pass defense): Michigan’s offense averages 7.4 yards per pass attempt, and Penn State’s defense allows 5.3 yards per pass attempt (FBS average 7.5).
When Michigan has the ball (third down): Michigan’s offense converts 38.3% of its third downs, and Penn State’s defense allows opponents to convert 26.4% of their third downs (FBS average 39.6%).
EdgeDesk’s position-group ratings put Penn State’s secondary No. 6 nationally and Michigan’s No. 79.
contradicting: When Michigan has the ball (big plays on the ground): Michigan’s offense turns 4.0% of its runs into explosive gains, and Penn State’s defense gives up explosive gains on 12.8% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.6%).

When Penn State has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Penn State’s offense has allowed a sack on 3.8% of its dropbacks, and Michigan’s defense sacks the quarterback on 8.5% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).
When Penn State has the ball (the run game against the run defense): Penn State’s offense averages 4.4 yards per carry, and Michigan’s defense allows 3.5 yards per carry (FBS average 5.1).

When Penn State has the ball (big plays on the ground): Penn State’s offense turns 4.3% of its runs into explosive gains, and Michigan’s defense gives up explosive gains on 1.5% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.6%).
quarterbacks: Bryce Underwood has completed 67 of 115 passes (58.3%) for 881 yards, 7.7 yards per attempt, 5 touchdowns and 4 interceptions in five games for Michigan, and has been sacked on 8 of 123 dropbacks.
Rocco Becht has completed 83 of 135 passes (61.5%) for 1,113 yards, 8.2 yards per attempt, 10 touchdowns and 3 interceptions in five games for Penn State, and has been sacked on 6 of 141 dropbacks.
